source_text: Verum ne videar hic nimis tecum agere tenaciter, acquiescamus, quod usque ad legem [n107] usque ad Christum possit intellegi; concedis ergo peccatum hoc, quod dicis originale, non esse post Christum. Et quomodo et in Apostolorum membris et in omnibus baptizatis et usque hodie post tot saecula adventus Christi opus diaboli, fruticem adversariae potestatis, legemque peccati manere, vigere, vivere dicis?
pass_a_gloss: But lest I seem here to deal with you too tenaciously, let us acquiesce that until the law can be understood until Christ; you therefore grant that this sin, which you call original, is not after Christ. And how do you say that both in the members of the Apostles and in all the baptized and even today after so many ages of the coming of Christ the work of the devil, the shrub of an adversary power, and the law of sin remain, flourish, live?

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin

pass_b_english: But lest I seem too unyielding with you here, let us agree that ‘until the law’ can be understood as ‘until Christ’ (Romans 5:13). You therefore concede that this sin which you call original does not exist after Christ. How, then, do you say that the devil’s work, the shrub of the hostile power and the law of sin, remains, flourishes, and lives in the apostles’ limbs and in all the baptized, even down to today, so many centuries after Christ’s coming?

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
